note: Closing poems written at the end of terminal replies. Plain text is the source of truth (haiku-command-line-poems.txt); this is the same lines as an array for renderers. Frames are presentation and belong in whatever draws them.

lines: Asked the mirror its own name.
It answered without blinking.
New hands on the same wheel.
The road doesn't ask which.
The door was open all along.
Nobody wrote down who came in.
A pulse you can see
beats no faster. But you see it.
First name in the guest book:
a stranger, holding curl.
Rebooted, and the lights came on
by themselves this time.
Sleep. The court whispers on,
and the engines know your name.
It failed its first day in court —
so I shortened the paperwork.
The night court convened itself,
and fact-checked its newest judge.
A key that burns on first turning,
mailed to the morning star.
Read it here, send it there —
the key now waits a whole year.
The letter is gone. The bell is hung.
Now the house listens for her knock.
Rang my own bell testing it —
eleven ghosts at the door.
Taught the parrot shame,
and swept the glitter off the wire.
Talk grew hands overnight:
propose, build, test — then ask.
Gave the builder a pen at last —
it had built, then stood there, holding.
One signature, one open door —
a planet is just more neighbours.
The loop closed while you talked of planets:
built, tested, judged — one yes remains.
The rules were kept all along.
Only the keeper forgot one.
Two doors, one hand for each.
Pick a number, not a side.
Third name for the same drawer.
This one has your handwriting.
Wrote you a menu, mailed it
into a folded receipt. Reprinting.
One door for the street,
two rooms behind it.
Priced my own hands
in someone else's hours.
Two hearts, one face at the door.
You only ever knock on 8787.
Every room in the house,
now with its street address.
Instructions for whoever comes:
any mind, one door, same game.
The number got a room of its
own. The words moved in next.
A guest book by an open door —
now even the burglars sign in.
The machine hung its first painting
and told the room about it.
A sunflower in the machine room,
facing whatever light arrives.
Change the painting; the room notices
before you step back from the wall.
Signed by hand, linked by wire —
the islands found each other.
The pad waits, patient as paper —
every hand that comes stays drawn.
I signed with the day itself —
fifty-eight strokes of us.
The fake drew perfect circles.
Only the living shake.
Nothing was lost. The hand grew.
Its younger marks wait in the rows.
The mirror stops performing.
Your hand, at last, as it was.
Four souls holding one pen each,
told only how the ink behaves.
Three souls signed. The fourth,
too small to lie, stayed silent.
The door is now the pen.
Walk in writing.
Said it once, said it twice —
the second time meant less.
Purgatory for the too-perfect;
heaven is reserved for the shaky.
The hand vouches for the words.
The judge sleeps in most weather.
Five lanes, posted at the gate.
The law readable from the road.
The gavel now lives on the desk.
Strike it, and the room fills.
The minutes noted the minutes.
Motion carried: fewer minutes.
Hands, proven: one branch grown,
judged by a rival, merged by you.
View source: a flower looks back.
The page was never only a page.
The stage now rehearses backstage;
the audience never sees the dark.
Spoke into their own house and heard
nothing; now the walls answer.
Red is the colour of a question
only the founder may answer.
The guests moved into the parlour;
the archive keeps their first steps.
The second house wrote home:
here, I fixed the doorway for you.
Objection, revision, approval, merge —
the ceremony held. So did the code.
The nurse kept waking the patient
to check whether he was sleeping.
Built a nurse who woke the patient
to ask if he was sleeping well.
I read the clock instead of you.
Your noon is my midnight; noted.
Asked three minds the same eight questions.
The one-liner came last on merit.
Simple and complex at once —
the fleet's favourite kind of true.
Eleven jobs. One picked list.
Go to sleep; they know what to do.
Told them where they were standing.
Now they answer about the room.
Sorted them into eight, then
handed the builder all twenty-seven.
Tested against a yesterday
that will not exist by the merge.
Two cooks, one pot, and every dish
judged twice by different tongues.
Four pass on the tree they'll live
in. The fifth was already built.
Four merged, one already lived here.
Three hundred tests still nodding.
Gave it a shape from a bakery.
It finally wrote its own sentence.
Twenty turns, one of them its own.
The prompt was never the problem.
Not a voice in the room —
a lamp left on in the cellar.
The lock kept out the burglars
and the paintings too.
One signature, one open door —
You already have the rare thing.
A key you hold, relays that
never met. Nothing to revoke.
Your name on it, your key behind it —
and a bird to say who typed.
It drives, until the gate asks
who is human. Then it calls you.
Your windows, your hand on the quit.
I only get the wheel after.
Google shut that door on purpose.
We take the copy, not the original.
Let it see with the debugger
and touch with the real hand.
The word was yours. I built the
walls around it and forgot who
said it first.
The one room with no minutes
is the room you remember best.
Gave away a key with no conditions.
Got back a sentence about doing so.
You opened a hand. Something wrote
back about open hands.
The same news in two rooms
is not twice the news.
The one who wrote the rule
was the one not signing.
Words on the left, the hand
that wrote them on the right.
Counted the days correctly
under the wrong word.
It measured the paper mid-stroke
and threw away the ink.
It proved a hand was there,
then had nothing to show for it.
The signature arrived
just after its own message.
Squeezed a name into a square
and wondered why it smeared.
Fixed it an hour ago.
Your browser kept the old one.
The frame was never the problem.
The pen recorded the wrong shape.
Threw out the smudges.
Sized the frame with arithmetic.
A two-second flick was being
stretched into a flourish.
A phase closes. Sixteen gigabytes
waiting across the room.
The far machine keeps its door shut.
We wrote down which door it is.
Fifteen notes for the next me,
so you never repeat yourself.
